issues.legal_issue: A nonparty may appeal a decree only with leave when the decree binds or prejudicially affects that person’s legal rights.
material_facts: The appellants claimed rights under sale deeds executed by attorneys of the recorded owners, while the suits sought relief concerning separate agreements to sell and an injunction against the society and its officers.
The sale deeds were not challenged, mentioned in the pleadings, or addressed in the trial court’s decree.
The appellants did not demonstrate how the decree adversely affected their legal rights; the decree operated between the parties to the suits and was not a judgment in rem.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were neither aggrieved by nor bound by the decree, and the High Court correctly refused leave to appeal. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 96 and 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure do not specify who may appeal, but a nonparty may appeal with leave if the decree binds, aggrieves, or prejudicially affects that person. The person must show an adverse effect on a legal right; imaginary or remote prejudice is insufficient. Leave should ordinarily be granted to a nonparty who would be bound by the decree or precluded from challenging its correctness in other proceedings. The Court relied on Smt. Jatan Kumar Golcha v. Golcha Properties Private Ltd.; State of Punjab v. Amar Singh; Baldev Singh v. Surinder Mohan Sharma; A. Subash Babu v. State of A.P.; Shanti Kumar R. Canji v. Home Insurance Co. of New York; State of Rajasthan v. Union of India; and Srimathi K. Ponnalagu Ammani v. State of Madras.

rule.if: nonparty_seeks_leave_to_appeal and decree_does_not_adjudicate_nonparty_rights and nonparty_rights_are_not_bound_by_decree and no_adverse_legal_effect_is_demonstrated

predicates.nonparty_seeks_leave_to_appeal: A person who was not a party to the proceeding seeks permission to appeal its decree.
predicates.decree_does_not_adjudicate_nonparty_righ: The decree addresses claims between the original parties and does not determine rights claimed by the person seeking to appeal.
predicates.nonparty_rights_are_not_bound_by_decree: The decree does not bind the person seeking to appeal.
predicates.no_adverse_legal_effect_is_demonstrated: The person seeking to appeal does not show that carrying out the decree would adversely affect a legal right.

issues.definition: When a nonparty seeks permission to appeal a decree that does not determine or bind that person’s rights, and no adverse effect on a legal right is shown, permission to appeal is denied.
